
=== story.oldMillRoad ===
TRIAL 26 CRS 005000 · State of North Carolina v. Belinda Park
  Charges: Felony Death by Vehicle; Reckless Driving
  Defendant: Belinda Park, 29, Line cook; priors: 0; Released on a $75,000 secured bond; missed one court date early on, then was re-released.
  TEMPLATE story.oldMillRoad
  Summary: At about 11:52 p.m. on 25 May, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Port Hollis and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The Corolla's driver, David Bergstrom, 34, a nurse driving home from a twelve-hour shift, died at the scene. Belinda Park, a line cook at The Copper Kettle, had stayed after closing that night. A hospital blood test about ninety minutes after the crash and a second, State Crime Laboratory test about three hours after it disagree on whether Park was over the legal limit when the cars collided. Park says a deer came out of the tree line and she swerved.
  Verdicts: Felony Death by Vehicle: notGuilty; Reckless Driving: notGuilty
  Reaction: District Attorney Dora Alvarez: "The court has spoken. Our office will keep standing up for safety on our roads."
  Reaction: Miriam Bryson: "Park has lived under this charge for a long time. It's over."
  Reaction: David Bergstrom's sister, outside the courtroom: "We'll be living with this. Park gets to walk away."
  Reaction: Park's grandmother: "We can finally breathe. Thank you for listening."
  News: Judge acquits Park in felony death by vehicle case — In a ruling from the bench, Judge Hale acquitted Park of felony death by vehicle. According to court records, at about 11:52 p.m. on 25 May, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Port Hollis and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. Reaction outside the courthouse was split. Park's grandmother: "We can finally breathe. Thank you for listening." District Attorney Dora Alvarez: "The court has spoken. Our office will keep standing up for safety on our roads." Miriam Bryson: "Park has lived under this charge for a long time. It's over." The case was heard over 2 days.

TRIAL 26 CRS 005010 · State of North Carolina v. Antonia Beaumont
  Charges: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)
  Defendant: Antonia Beaumont, 46, School bus mechanic; priors: 14; Released on a $500,000 secured bond; missed one court date early on, then was re-released.
  TEMPLATE story.churchBooks
  Summary: For six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. When a new trustee asked for the building fund statements, $112,400 was gone, moved over three years in 41 checks and transfers to an account in the name of "DL Property Services." Beaumont says Pastor Harold Peebles approved every payment as short-term loans to the contractor rebuilding the fellowship hall, and that the paperwork was handshakes. The pastor, now retired and in poor health, says no such arrangement existed.
  Verdicts: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more): lesser
  [Count 1: Embezzlement] Class D Felony, prior record level V (habitual felon; offense is Class H felony) | Presumptive range | Minimum 89, maximum 119 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.

Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Projected release: no earlier than 20 April 2034, and no later than 20 October 2035. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Total: US$213.00
  Reaction: ADA Cynthia Vasquez: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust."
  Reaction: Cassidy Merritt: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps."
  Reaction: A former employer of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over."
  News: Verdict in ‘$112,000 and a Handshake’ case: guilty — Superior Court Judge Hale found Antonia Beaumont, 46, guilty, and imposed 89 to 119 months in prison, ending a case that began with an arrest in Wexley. According to court records, for six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. Reaction outside the courthouse was split. A former employer of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over." ADA Cynthia Vasquez: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust." Cassidy Merritt: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps." Chris Yates, a registered nurse, worked every one of those nights and had pulled insulin from the medication cabinet for patients who didn't need it.   Verdicts: First-Degree Murder: guilty; First-Degree Murder: guilty; First-Degree Murder: lesser; Attempted First-Degree Murder: guilty; Obstruction of Justice: notGuilty

Their bodies were found the next day in the woods across the creek, throats cut. The case went unsolved for five years. An unspent .40-caliber round found between the girls' bodies was matched to a pistol in Vega's home. In jail, Vega confessed more than 60 times to guards, a psychologist, and his spouse on the phone. Vega says the confessions came from a breakdown in solitary confinement and that the killings were done by others.

  TEMPLATE story.hazingDeath
  Summary: On 24 February, Percy Alvarado, 19, a pledge at a fraternity near the university in Wexley, was made to run a "gauntlet" of drinking stations, downing nearly a bottle and a half of vodka in under two hours. His blood alcohol later measured 0.36. He fell headfirst down the basement stairs. Brothers carried him to a couch. The house's own security cameras show him struggling for twelve hours: falling, trying to stand, hitting his head again, while brothers walked past. At one point Willoughby slapped him and poured a cup of liquid on his face. No one called 911 until the next morning. He died of a ruptured spleen and brain injuries. Nestor Willoughby, the pledge master who organized the gauntlet, is one of several brothers charged. Someone deleted footage from the cameras after the death; the police recovered it.

  Charges: Voluntary Manslaughter
  Defendant: Lyle Matthis, 27, Rideshare driver; priors: 0; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $225,000 secured bond for 38 days.
  TEMPLATE story.fatalPunchParty
  Summary: At a backyard cookout on 20 June, Zachariah Dickens and Lyle Matthis argued over an insult about a family member. Lyle Matthis punched Zachariah Dickens once, and Zachariah Dickens fell onto a stone patio. Zachariah Dickens died at the hospital the next day. Matthis says Zachariah Dickens shoved him first and he never meant to hurt anyone.
  Verdicts: Voluntary Manslaughter: guilty
  [Count 1: Voluntary Manslaughter] Class D Felony, prior record level I | Presumptive range | Minimum 51, maximum 74 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.
  [Commitment] Minimum term to be served before the defendant is eligible for release: 51 months (4 yr 3 mo). | Maximum term: 74 months. Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Credit for 38 days already served in pretrial confinement (G.S. 15-196.1). | Projected release: no earlier than 13 January 2031, and no later than 13 December 2031. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Restitution: US$10,000.00 | State Crime Laboratory fee: US$600.00 | Total: US$10,813.00
  [Victim notification] The District Attorney's victim-witness legal assistant will notify the victim of the judgment and of any release, appeal, or post-conviction hearing (N.C. Const. art. I, § 37).
  Reaction: ADA Gilbert Kincaid: "No verdict undoes the harm. But this one says it mattered."
  Reaction: Elise Prescott: "We respect the court, even though we see the evidence differently."
  Reaction: A family friend of the Dickens family, outside the courtroom: "It's not enough. It's never going to be enough."
  Reaction: Matthis's grandmother: "We'll be waiting when it's over."
  News: Verdict in ‘Guest Dies After Single Punch at Birthday Gathering’ case: guilty — Superior Court Judge Hale found Lyle Matthis, 27, guilty, and imposed 51 to 74 months in prison, ending a case that began with an arrest in Wexley. According to court records, at a backyard cookout on 20 June, Zachariah Dickens and Lyle Matthis argued over an insult about a family member. Opinions in the hallway afterward were as divided as the evidence. ADA Gilbert Kincaid: "No verdict undoes the harm. But this one says it mattered." A family friend of the Dickens family, outside the courtroom: "It's not enough. It's never going to be enough." Elise Prescott: "We respect the court, even though we see the evidence differently." Matthis was taken into custody in the courtroom. Counting 38 days already served, the earliest possible release is 13 January 2031. The judgment includes US$10,813.00 in fines, fees, costs, and restitution.
